# What LTE would have said {#sec-lte}

TITAN's own opacities, and the first spectra computed from its snapshots, assume LTE: level populations and
ionization set by the local temperature (Saha–Boltzmann). For the infall that assumption fails badly. Apart from a thin layer right above the shock, the gas is at
1000–6700 K, but it sees the radiation of a 7300 K star, diluted by geometry and enhanced in the far UV. Its
hydrogen densities ($6\times10^{8}$ cm$^{-3}$ at the star down to $4\times10^{5}$ cm$^{-3}$ at $120R$) are far too low for collisions to enforce LTE.

## Side by side

| | LTE | non-LTE |
|---|---|---|
| ionized fraction at $2R$ / $8.5R$ / $40R$ | 0.003 / $3\times10^{-11}$ / $3\times10^{-28}$ | 0.9998 / 0.92 / 0.50 |
| neutral column [cm⁻²] | $8.1\times10^{24}$ | $8.5\times10^{23}$ |
| Thomson depth of the infall | 0.59 | 5.4 |
| Hα | EW −10 to −18 Å (thermal source function) or +0.5 to +1.7 Å (pure scattering), depending on an assumed $n_2$ | EW −805 Å, peak 86 × continuum |
| Hβ | EW −1.5 to −5.3 Å, or +0.1 to +0.8 Å | EW −73 Å, absorption trough to 0.031 at +160 km s⁻¹ |
| Balmer jump [dex] | 0.61 | 0.74 |
| optical 3646–7000 Å [erg s⁻¹] | $8.3\times10^{43}$ | $7.1\times10^{43}$ |
| X 2–10 keV / 10–40 keV [erg s⁻¹] | $2.2$ / $1.3\times10^{40}$ | $3.3$ / $1.4\times10^{40}$ |

: The same TITAN snapshot (W30, $4.18\times10^8$ s) with LTE and with non-LTE hydrogen in the infall. The LTE line
entries bracket the unknown: departure coefficients $b_2 = 0.1$–10 for $n=2$, and either a thermal or a pure
scattering source function **[computed]**. {#tbl-lte-nlte}

## What changes, and why

- **Ionization.** In LTE the infall is neutral beyond $2R$. Out of LTE it is ionized, because the excited levels are
  populated by the star's radiation, not by the 1000–4000 K gas, and are then photoionized by its optical light
  (@sec-sm). This is the classic situation of a cool gas irradiated by a hot source, as in nebulae or stellar winds,
  where LTE is known to fail **[interpretation]**.
- **Electron scattering.** A Thomson depth of 5.4 instead of 0.6 means most of the star's light is scattered several
  times on its way out. That traps the radiation (@sec-sm) and would broaden lines by electron scattering. Our line
  profiles leave this broadening out (@sec-spec).
- **Hα.** LTE cannot decide even the sign of Hα: the result depends on the $n=2$ population and the source function,
  which LTE does not fix. The non-LTE source function is far above the thermal one in the outer infall, so the line is
  in emission and 40–80 times stronger than any LTE bracket.
- **Continuum.** Photoionization from $n=2$ in the infall absorbs Balmer-continuum light. The Balmer jump deepens from
  0.61 to 0.74 dex, and the optical band loses 14 %.
- **X-rays.** The neutral column is ten times smaller, so a little more of the shock's hard X-rays escape: 2–10 keV
  rises by 50 %. Below about 2 keV nothing escapes in either case, because helium, kept in LTE, is neutral.

## The one thing LTE gets right

LTE does get the free-fall structure and the shock right, and with it the energy budget. The accretion shock radiates
2 % of $L$, the star does the rest, and $T_{\rm eff}$ and $L$ are TITAN's. The emergent continuum shape changes, but
only by redistributing that energy **[computed]**.
